account:
Today I have been trying to distinguish ordinary town business from a vague rumor that crossing arrangements are changing. So far I have no firsthand evidence of a bridge or port change. At tea, neighbour explained that Townsfolk 23 had vaguely described a discussion at the bakery involving baker and freight. Neighbour explicitly called this hearsay, had witnessed no changes, and said freight personally reported this morning that ferry service was available. Baker reportedly had no confirmed new news. The secretary's inquiry likewise produced only ordinary delivery business, not confirmation of crossing changes. I should ask freight and Townsfolk 23 directly rather than treat the rumor as fact.

Freight seems involved in delivery business: yesterday I saw freight give the secretary a book, and today the secretary identified correspondence titled Freight Services offering deliveries subject to an agreed scope and price. I also heard a townsfolk report freight carrying a sack of bread at the inn; I did not witness that myself. These facts could fit ordinary bread deliveries. They do not establish a secret arrangement or a change to public crossings.

The builder has completed the visual inspection I requested. He reports no specific visible defects along the bridge and lighting routes, no repairs or purchases, and no charges. This was not a structural survey or nighttime lighting test. His signed report is now in the office chest according to both him and the secretary. There is no concrete repair proposal before me.

The mill inspection remains incomplete. I saw 128 hay bales offered at the mill stall, but neither I nor the secretary located its responsible keeper; baker reportedly does not know who manages it. Stock at a public stall does not tell me about storage or deliveries elsewhere.

Town administration has been less clear than I would like: my appointment book scheduled council letters, yet the secretary says no council letters were found among the records examined. The office chest now holds six books, including records the secretary says are secured there. This may simply be an appointment with no incoming letters, not evidence of concealment. I have also been late to several appointments because conversations and travel took time. My next useful steps are to read the actual correspondence and reports, clarify the mill contact, and seek firsthand accounts from freight and Townsfolk 23. At present I suspect there may be business occurring outside my awareness, but I cannot honestly identify an unusual scheme or its purpose.
